article_title: Computational Thinking Boosters: Algorithmic Thinking in K-2
citation: Computational Thinking Boosters: Algorithms in K-2. (2021). Webinar presentation, NSF grant #1923314. https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=1923314
title: Recognize and name the algorithmic thinking already present in K-2 daily routines
description: The webinar asks teachers to consider "Where Am I Likely Already Integrating These Skills?" and notes that many K-2 skills are algorithmic in nature: following a daily schedule, collaboratively creating classroom procedures through testing and analyzing outcomes, and conversations about how sequence order affects outcomes. Teachers should surface these existing practices as computational thinking rather than adding wholly new content.
requirements: Teacher awareness of decomposition, pattern recognition, comparing and contrasting in existing routines
target_learning_goals: Recognizing algorithmic thinking in daily life
examples: Students and teachers collaborate to create classroom procedures through testing and analyzing outcomes
key_sources: Computational Thinking Boosters: Algorithms in K-2. (2021). Webinar presentation, NSF grant #1923314. https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=1923314

article_title: Comparison of the problem based learning-driven with the traditional didactic-lecture-based curricula.
citation: Zahid Muhammad A., Varghese Ramani, Mohammed Ahmed M., Ayed Adel K. (2016). Comparison of the problem based learning-driven with the traditional didactic-lecture-based curricula. International Journal of Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.5116/ijme.5749.80f5
title: Use suitably designed K2-type MCQs to assess higher-cognitive knowledge acquired in PBL settings
description: The article concludes that "Suitably designed MCQs can be used to tap the higher cognitive knowledge base acquired in the PBL setting". Because K2-type items require selecting the most correct answer among options of varying correctness, the authors argue they measure comprehension, analysis, integration and application, unlike K1 recall items. They position this as a novel approach for comparing PBL with lecture-based teaching, while calling for further methodologically sound studies to establish the usefulness of K2-type MCQs for measuring deeper understanding.
requirements: MCQs developed in accordance with a blueprint derived from weekly learning objectives
Blind cross-checking of item categorization by independent subject experts
Post-test item analysis to detect miss-keyed items or writing flaws
constraints: The authors state further methodologically sound studies are needed to establish the usefulness of K2 type MCQs for measuring higher cognitive levels
target_learning_goals: assessing higher-cognitive knowledge base in curriculum comparisons
examples: The 2011-12 examination consisted of 225 MCQs categorized by independent subject experts, with reliability coefficient 0.8
key_sources: Zahid Muhammad A., Varghese Ramani, Mohammed Ahmed M., Ayed Adel K. (2016). Comparison of the problem based learning-driven with the traditional didactic-lecture-based curricula. International Journal of Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.5116/ijme.5749.80f5
